anomalies.observed: R71 is a bleeder/protection resistor across VOUTP/VOUTN. Its value field is '24k', but its description and MPN ('FRC0805J240TSD') specify a 24Ω part.
anomalies.expected: R71 should be a 24kΩ resistor (as the value field indicates). A 24Ω part would draw excessive current and dissipate far too much power across the VOUTP/VOUTN rail.

evidence.quote: (comp (ref "R71") (value "24k") ... (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS") ... (field (name "MPN") "FRC0805J240TSD"))

anomalies.impact: If the board is assembled from the MPN/description, a 24Ω resistor will be installed, causing a near-short across the VOUTP/VOUTN rail, high power dissipation, and likely damage.

anomalies.observed: For the isolated CAN transceivers U14 and U52, logic-side ground (GND1, pin 4) and bus-side ground (GND2, pin 5) are both tied to the same global GND net. Their bus-side supply VCC2 is powered from the non-isolated 5V_switched_CAN rail.
anomalies.expected: The specification calls for 'two isolated CAN buses ... through an isolated CAN transceiver'. Galvanic isolation requires GND1 and GND2 to remain separate, with VCC2 supplied by an isolated rail.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN buses are not galvanically isolated; ground loops and common-mode voltages can couple between the CM4 side and the CAN bus side, defeating the intended isolation and potentially causing communication errors or damage.

anomalies.observed: The switchable CAN termination is miswired. R96 (120Ω) connects CANL0 (/NET0165) to SW8 pin 1; R13 (120Ω) connects CANL1 (/NET0155) to SW8 pin 2. SW8 pin 3 is CANH1 (/NET0106) and pin 4 is CANH0 (/NET0078). Since SW8 is a 2-section DIP switch (pins 1-2 and 3-4 only), closing either section cannot place a 120Ω resistor across CANH/CANL of either bus.
anomalies.expected: Each CAN bus should be terminable by a 120Ω resistor between its CANH and CANL lines when the corresponding DIP switch section is closed (e.g., SW8.1=R96 to CANL0, SW8.2=CANH0; SW8.3=R13 to CANL1, SW8.4=CANH1).
anomalies.impact: The onboard switchable termination cannot properly terminate either CAN bus. If left unterminated, signal integrity may be poor, especially on longer buses, causing communication errors.

The CAN termination switch is also miswired.
